error.bad_output: The command finished without a readable result; it may have been interrupted. Try again, and if it keeps happening, run tavotto codex doctor in a terminal for the raw output.
error.canvas_incomplete: The installed plugin is incomplete: its embedded canvas is missing or damaged, or doesn't match the bundled manifest. The tools still work in Codex, just without a canvas. Reinstall the plugin (codex plugin remove tavotto@tavotto, then codex plugin add tavotto@tavotto), then run the install again. Nothing was changed this time.
error.cli_not_found: Couldn't find the Tavotto command line (tavotto-cli) on this machine. The install may be incomplete — reinstalling the desktop app fixes it.
error.codex_cli_missing: Couldn't find the codex command. Install the Codex CLI yourself first, then try again.

doctor.interpreter_unusable: The plugin’s launcher command can’t run on this machine, so Codex would show no tools. This run only diagnosed and changed nothing; installing switches to an interpreter verified to run.
doctor.marketplace_add_failed: Tavotto isn't registered as a Codex plugin marketplace yet. This run only diagnosed, so nothing changed; running the install sets it up.
doctor.plugin_add_failed: The plugin isn't installed yet. This run only diagnosed, so nothing changed; running the install sets it up.
doctor.provision_failed: The plugin doesn't have a matching version of the Tavotto engine yet. This run only diagnosed, so nothing changed; running the install sets it up.

error.engine_too_old: The Tavotto engine on this machine is older than the minimum the installed plugin requires, so the plugin's bridge can't drive it. Upgrade the engine (pipx upgrade tavotto, or update the desktop app), or roll the plugin back to a version that matches.
error.health_failed: Everything is installed, but the health check failed — the plugin still can't find a usable Tavotto engine. Expand the details below for what it reported.
error.interpreter_unusable: The plugin’s launcher command can’t run on this machine, so Codex would show no tools. On Windows, python3 is often the Microsoft Store placeholder: it appears installed but exits immediately. Installing switches to an interpreter verified to run; if none is found, install Python or set TAVOTTO_MCP_PYTHON and try again.
error.marketplace_add_failed: Couldn't register Tavotto as a Codex plugin marketplace. Usually there's no network access, or no permission to write Codex's config directory.
error.marketplace_state_unknown: Couldn't determine Codex's marketplace registration (codex plugin marketplace list produced no result), so nothing was changed. That's not the same as not registered. Expand the details for what Codex reported: usually the codex command can't start from inside Tavotto (for example an npm-installed codex that can't find node), or Codex itself isn't set up yet.
error.not_desktop: This action is only available in the desktop app.
error.other: The install didn't succeed. The command's own words are in the details below.
error.pin_failed: Couldn’t write the new launcher command to both manifests, so it was rolled back. The plugin directory may be read-only or in use — fix that and try again.
error.plugin_add_failed: The marketplace was registered, but the plugin wasn’t installed. Expand the details below for what Codex reported.
error.plugin_install_ambiguous: Couldn’t locate a single installed plugin. Codex reported no install path, and the cache has zero or several same-named copies. Expand the details for the candidates; usually codex plugin remove tavotto@tavotto then codex plugin add tavotto@tavotto clears it up.
error.plugin_source_unsupported: The marketplace is registered, but Codex doesn’t list the Tavotto plugin. This Codex version may not understand the plugin source in the marketplace manifest, or the local snapshot may be stale. Run codex plugin marketplace upgrade tavotto in a terminal first; if the plugin still doesn’t appear, update Codex.
error.plugin_state_unknown: Couldn’t determine the plugin’s install state, so nothing was changed. That’s not the same as not installed. Expand the details for what Codex reported.
error.provision_failed: The plugin is installed, but its matching Tavotto engine couldn’t be prepared.
error.spawn_failed: Couldn’t start the Tavotto command line. Try again, or run tavotto codex install in a terminal for the raw output.
error.uninstall_failed: The removal didn’t finish. The command’s own words are in the details below.

updateNotice.intro: Update to get this release’s new features and fixes.
updateNotice.installed: {{version}} is installed. This window still runs the old version — restart to use it.
updateNotice.upgraded: Upgraded to {{version}}. Restart Tavotto to use it.
updateNotice.failed: Couldn’t update. You’re still on the current version.
updateNotice.sourceBody: This is a source checkout, so Tavotto doesn’t upgrade itself. Run this in the repository:

versions.compareDescription: Base = this version; translucent outline = current canvas
versions.compareTip: Large overlay comparison (base = this version, outline = current)
versions.deleteBody: Deleted versions can’t be recovered. Your current document isn’t affected.

diff.overridesDetail: {{name}}: {{elements}} figure elements changed (position {{pos}}, text {{text}}, axes layout {{axes}}, other {{other}})

versions.keepTitle: Automatic checkpoints are cleaned up over time. Keep one and it stays, like a manual version.
versions.noDiff: No differences from the current canvas
versions.previewApproximate: Figure-edit preview unavailable. The thumbnail below shows the original file.
versions.restoreMissingCanvasBody: This checkpoint came from canvas “{{from}}”, now deleted. Continuing writes into the current canvas “{{to}}”, replacing what’s there.
versions.restoreOtherCanvasBody: This checkpoint was taken on canvas “{{from}}”; you’re on “{{to}}”. Restoring switches to “{{from}}” and writes there, leaving the current canvas alone.
versions.restoreUnknownCanvasBody: It was left by an older version and doesn’t record its canvas. Continuing writes into the current canvas “{{to}}”, replacing what’s there.
versions.restoreUnknownCanvasTitle: This checkpoint has no source canvas
versions.restored: Restored document version “{{name}}”. You can undo this; no source file was touched.
versions.saved: Current document saved as a new version

summary.sameMetrics: Same object count and figure size

versions.title: Document versions

onboarding.targetWaiting: Waiting for the target to appear…
onboarding.targetMissing: The target for this step is not on screen.

precondition.editPanelMissing: {{name}}, the figure this tutorial edits, is not on this canvas. Open it first.
precondition.notInElementEdit: This step happens inside the figure editor of {{name}}. Open it first.
precondition.noTextSelected: Select text in the figure first — the title or an axis label.
precondition.editPanelNotRendered: {{name}} has not been rendered yet, so the Problems panel has no results for it. Open it once first.
precondition.otherPanelMissing: Only one tutorial figure is on the canvas; aligning needs at least two. Add {{name}} first.
precondition.notInLayout: Multi-select happens in the canvas layout. Go back to the canvas first.

onboarding.hintsReset: Contextual hints reset; each will show once more

failure.unavailable: Tutorial resources are incomplete. Reinstall Tavotto.
failure.open_failed: Couldn’t open the tutorial project. Try again, or open your own project.
failure.locked: A file in the tutorial project is in use by another program. Close it and try again.
failure.document_failed: Couldn’t read the tutorial canvas — incompatible version or missing file. Try “Reset tutorial project”.
failure.no_api: This environment does not provide the tutorial.

reset.title: Reset the tutorial project?
reset.body: The tutorial project goes back to how it was installed. Your edits, written-back figures, and progress are cleared; other projects are untouched.
reset.bodyWithLayouts: The tutorial project goes back to how it was installed, and the canvas files you saved in it are cleared too: {{names}}. Export them first to keep them; other projects are untouched.

welcome.title: Learn Tavotto with a sample
welcome.body: An offline tutorial copy: edit freely and restart any time; your own projects are never affected. Next, you’ll walk through the two core workflows.

open_fast_edit.title: Open a figure
open_fast_edit.body: Double-click Fig2_correlation in the “Assets” drawer on the left to edit inside the figure.

canvas.title: Open a figure
canvas.body: Double-click Fig2_correlation on the canvas to edit inside the figure. Its card in the “Assets” drawer works too.

select_text.title: Select text
select_text.body: Click the title or an axis label inside the figure to select it.

change_typography.title: Change the size or font
change_typography.body: In the properties on the right, change the font size or family, for example make it larger. Every change goes into undo history.

locate_problem.title: Locate from “Problems”
locate_problem.body: Open “Problems” on the left; it lists what breaks the spec in this figure.

row.title: Locate from “Problems”
row.body: Click a problem; Tavotto selects the object and focuses the matching property field.

export_original.title: Look at the original export
export_original.body: Open “Export”, confirm the scope is “Original size”, then close the panel.

scope.title: Look at the original export
scope.body: “Original size” outputs the figure at its own size, unaffected by canvas scaling. Close the panel to continue.

add_to_layout.title: Add to canvas
add_to_layout.body: Both figures are already on the canvas. Click “Add to canvas” to go back to the layout and see them.

missing.title: Add to canvas
missing.body: {{name}} isn’t on the canvas yet. Add it from the “Assets” drawer on the left; this step completes once both figures are on the layout.

multi_select_align.title: Shift-select
multi_select_align.body: Hold Shift and click the second figure to select both.

bar.title: Align
bar.body: Pick an alignment in the floating bar next to the selection, for example align top.

export_canvas.title: Look at the canvas export
export_canvas.body: Open “Export” again, confirm the scope is “Canvas”, then close the panel.

scope.title: Look at the canvas export
scope.body: “Canvas” outputs the whole page using its size and layout. Close the panel to continue.

done.title: Tutorial complete
done.body: You’ve covered quick edit, locating problems, original and canvas export, and multi-select alignment. Reopen the tutorial any time from the “More” menu.

partial.title: Tutorial finished
partial.body: {{done}} of {{total}} steps done, {{skipped}} skipped. Reopen the tutorial from the “More” menu to revisit the skipped ones.

allSkipped.title: Tutorial ended
allSkipped.body: You skipped all {{total}} steps, so you haven’t tried quick edit, locating problems, export, or multi-select alignment yet. Reopen the tutorial from the “More” menu to walk through them.
